definition: A hydrocarbon with at least one carbon-carbon double bond; the family whose functional group C=C makes it far more reactive than the alkanes. General formula CnH2n.
msAccepts: hydrocarbon containing a C=C double bond
more reactive than alkanes because of the double bond
msAvoids: omitting the double bond from the definition

definition: A saturated hydrocarbon with only single carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bonds; the product family when an alkene is hydrogenated. General formula CnH2n+2.
msAccepts: product of adding hydrogen to an alkene
msAvoids: saying it contains a double bond

definition: The atom or bond arrangement that gives an organic family its characteristic reactions. The alkenes' functional group is the carbon-carbon double bond, written >C=C<.
msAccepts: the reactive part that determines chemical properties
msAvoids: giving the alkane skeleton as the alkene group

definition: A family of compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, a trend in physical properties, one general formula, and consecutive members differing by a -CH2- unit.
msAvoids: listing bullets without the functional-group thread

definition: A compound that contains carbon and hydrogen only. Both the alkanes and the alkenes are hydrocarbon families; the difference is the bonding between the carbons.
msAccepts: compound of carbon and hydrogen only
msAvoids: counting compounds with oxygen as hydrocarbons

definition: A drawing that shows every atom and every bond as an explicit line, including the double bond as two parallel lines. All four bonds at each carbon must be shown.
msAccepts: all atoms and all bonds drawn
C=C drawn as a double line
msAvoids: drawing the double bond as a single line

definition: A compound with the same molecular formula as another but a different structural formula. C4H8 has three alkene isomers: but-1-ene, but-2-ene and 2-methylpropene.
msAccepts: different arrangement of the same atoms
but-1-ene and but-2-ene as isomer pair

definition: A formula counting the atoms of each element in one molecule — C3H6 for propene — without showing how they are joined. For alkenes it always fits CnH2n.
msAccepts: shows what but not how joined

definition: A hydrocarbon containing at least one double or triple carbon-carbon bond. The alkenes are classified as unsaturated because they contain a C=C bond.
msAccepts: has double or triple C-C bonds
not maximum hydrogen because of the double bond (supporting only)

definition: A hydrocarbon with single carbon-carbon bonds only — no double (C=C) or triple (C≡C) bonds anywhere. The alkanes are the saturated family.
msAvoids: saying full of hydrogen as the definition

definition: One algebraic expression giving the molecular formula of every family member. For alkenes it is CnH2n: the hydrogen count is twice the carbon count.
msAccepts: one formula for all family members
msAvoids: mixing n with a fixed count

definition: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. Every alkene reduces to CH2, because the CnH2n pattern gives a fixed 1:2 carbon-to-hydrogen ratio.
msAvoids: giving C2H4 for ethene when the ratio is asked

definition: Burning in plenty of oxygen. For any hydrocarbon, including the alkenes, the products are carbon dioxide and water only.
msAccepts: burning in oxygen or air with plenty of oxygen
msAvoids: listing carbon monoxide or soot for complete combustion

definition: A reaction in which part of a double bond breaks to a single bond and atoms add across it: two reactant molecules become one product, and the double bond is consumed.
msAccepts: double bond breaks partially, atoms add across

definition: An alkane carrying two bromine atoms, formed when bromine adds across an alkene's double bond. Ethene gives 1,2-dibromoethane; propene gives 1,2-dibromopropane.
msAccepts: two Br atoms on adjacent carbons from bromine addition
product named x,2-dibromo... with the double bond consumed
msAvoids: leaving the C=C in the product

definition: An aqueous solution of bromine, orange in colour. Shaken with an unsaturated compound it goes colourless; with a saturated one the colour stays.
msAccepts: orange to colourless with a C=C compound
msAvoids: saying the mixture becomes clear instead of colourless

definition: The addition of hydrogen across a double bond: an alkene reacts with hydrogen to form an alkane. Used industrially to harden polyunsaturated plant oils into margarine.
msAccepts: addition of hydrogen to an alkene
msAvoids: leaving the product as an alkene

definition: The addition of water across a double bond: an alkene reacts with water (as steam) to form an alcohol. Ethene plus steam gives ethanol at 300 degrees C, 60-70 atmospheres, with a phosphoric acid catalyst.
msAccepts: addition of water to an alkene
steam, 300 degrees C, 60-70 atmospheres, phosphoric acid
msAvoids: naming an alkane as the product

definition: The alcohol C2H5OH, made industrially by hydrating ethene with steam over a phosphoric acid catalyst. The first member met of the alcohol family.
A substance that speeds a reaction without being consumed. Phosphoric acid catalyses the hydration of ethene; the bromine addition needs no catalyst at all.
msAvoids: saying it starts the reaction only
naming a catalyst for the bromine addition
